title: Healey’s Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds
summary:
There have been almost no Budget leaks.
The chancellor's aides are using intelligence-style security measures to guard its secrets: the Budget has been split into "compartments" with very few given access to all of them.
The IT has been locked down and ministers viewing the plans have to sign a digital promise not to brief media.
Such security is a response to the feeling that speculation around the last Budget, sometimes informed by insiders, was economically destabilising.
The economic news has been good - growth has been better than expected and the International Monetary Fund has endorsed the UK for "standing out" among the G7 countries for at least planning to cut borrowing.

title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
summary:
It's the only time I've lived near Aldi, the grocery store known for low prices.
Sponsor MessageAldi is a German company known for having low, low prices, and it deserves that reputation.
All to say: Aldi is disrupting the grocery business and actually lowering prices even as the cost of food—at restaurants and other grocery stores—goes up and up.
Aldi unbundled the part of the grocery business it can do super cheaply, and it intentionally locates Aldi stores near competitor grocery stores so shoppers can easily go grab the last few things on their list (the rest of the bundle).
I think the way Aldi's growth pressured competitors to keep prices low shows that grocers are not the right target of our ire over food prices.

title: Top Economist Says Rate Hike Not Needed, As Bond Market Is Doing Fed's Job
summary:
The "work" that Zandi sees the bond market doing is making borrowing costs higher, which is what the Fed aims to do when it tries to cool inflation.
Prior to the Fed's September rate increase, Zandi said that he viewed the decision as a "serious mistake" that could prove costly for the US economy.
A month later, the economist is still focused on the threats that further rate hikes could pose at a time when macro and geopolitical uncertainty remains high.
Zandi noted that global oil prices are surging back toward wartime peaks, as tensions with Iran show no signs of easing.
"Higher oil prices will further undermine real wages and, ultimately, consumer spending, something the Fed shouldn't dismiss," he added.

title: South Korea’s GDP growth beats forecasts amid AI boom
summary:
South Korea’s economy grew much faster than expected in the July-September quarter amid booming demand for chips used in artificial intelligence (AI).
Exports, which account for about 45 percent of South Korea’s GDP, rose 2.3 percent quarter-on-quarter, driven by semiconductors, machinery and electrical equipment, according to the central bank.
The latest results put the South Korean economy well on track to achieve its biggest economic expansion in more than a decade.
South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said earlier this month that he expected growth to reach 3.4-3.6 percent in 2026, which would be the strongest performance since 2011, excluding the COVID-19 pandemic.
South Korea’s economy grew 1 percent in 2025, its slowest expansion since the pandemic.
